acceptance_criteria.criterion: createMenu(config).run([]) launches interactive menu when TTY
Throws if any Command.key exceeds one character (S5)

summary: Created src/create-menu.ts with createMenu(config) factory returning { run(argv): Promise<number> }. Dispatch order: (1) pre-flight checks, (2) help command → printHelp returns 0, (3) setup command (when setupComponents defined) → runSetup, (4) direct command dispatch → cmd.run(flags), (5) unknown command → stderr error returns 1, (6) no command + TTY → showInteractiveMenu returns 0, (7) no command + no TTY → stderr error returns 1. Never calls process.exit().

S5 runtime validation: validateCommandKeys() checks every Command.key on construction — throws a descriptive error if any key has length !== 1. Called before the run() function is returned, so misconfigurations fail immediately at construction time.
Updated src/index.ts to re-export createMenu from create-menu.js, completing the public API barrel.

Created tests/create-menu.test.ts with 25 tests covering all 6 acceptance criteria: help dispatch, command dispatch (sync + async + flags), hidden command not dispatched, unknown command, interactive menu TTY/non-TTY, setup dispatch with components/without, pre-flight error handling, re-throw for non-PreflightError, and process.exit() never called verification.
All 207 tests pass, TypeScript clean, build produces correct dual CJS+ESM output. CJS require() resolves createMenu as a function.

comments.note: validateCommandKeys() is a pure internal helper that runs once at construction and never during run(). If a consumer constructs createMenu inside a hot path (e.g., per-request), they pay the O(n) validation cost repeatedly. The current usage pattern (singleton construction at startup) makes this a non-issue.

The setup dispatch (step 3) branches on 'config.setupComponents !== undefined'. If a consumer passes an empty array [], setup dispatch is active but runSetup() handles the empty case gracefully (returns 0 with dim message). The distinction between undefined and [] is consistent with the plan's intent.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified. Full suite of 207 tests (25 new in tests/create-menu.test.ts) passes with zero failures. TypeScript compiles clean (tsc --noEmit, no errors). Production build (tsup) succeeds — dual CJS+ESM output emitted. Runtime spot-checks confirm: (1) createMenu exported as function from both dist/index.cjs and dist/index.js; (2) S5 construction-time validation throws the correct error for a multi-char key; (3) null key is accepted without throwing. Static scan confirms process.exit() appears only in a JSDoc comment — never called at runtime.

comments.note: AC5 covers multi-char keys and empty-string keys; null keys are correctly permitted. No edge-case gaps detected in the validation logic.
No process.exit() call exists in src/create-menu.ts — confirmed by both the no-call test (vitest spy) and a static grep. Only occurrence is in the JSDoc comment.

summary: Reviewed src/create-menu.ts (112 lines), src/index.ts, and tests/create-menu.test.ts (25 tests). Implementation is clean, well-structured, and correctly implements all 6 ACs.
Dispatch order is clearly sequenced and matches the documented JSDoc. Construction-time key validation is the correct pattern — fails fast before run() is ever callable.
Pre-flight error handling correctly distinguishes PreflightError (soft exit via code) from arbitrary errors (re-throw). Consistent with the broader codebase error strategy.
Async command handling (sync-vs-Promise duck-typing) is correct; rejected Promises propagate to the caller as expected.
Hidden command guard (c.hidden filter in step 4 find) is a subtle correctness detail — well tested.
No blocking issues found. Two low-priority observations recorded as comments. One documentation-forward item for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: tests/create-menu.test.ts: Object.defineProperty(process.stdin, 'isTTY', ...) mutations are not cleaned up in afterEach. vi.restoreAllMocks() only restores vi.spyOn() calls. Since all tests that depend on isTTY set it themselves before asserting, this doesn't cause failures today — but it creates subtle order-dependence. Consider adding an afterEach restore or using a vi.stubEnv / Object.defineProperty callsite that resets to the original value.

src/create-menu.ts: The JSDoc dispatch order labels step 5 as 'Unknown command' but in the code this is handled inside the step 4 if-block (the find+undefined branch), not a separate top-level step. The comment is accurate in meaning but could mislead a reader into expecting a separate condition. Cosmetic only — no behavior impact.

[documentation-forward] src/index.ts comment says 'Phase B defers only the createMenu() entry point (create-menu.ts)' — this phrasing is stale once Phase B ships. The barrel is now complete. Documentation agent should update (or remove) the Phase A/B framing from the barrel comment so future readers see a stable, version-neutral description of what the index exports.
